title: People in the loop: two reviewers, agreement, gold labels, a contract change and re-scoring
design_ref: Semi-automatic verification: people in the loop; A verifier is a product (change and re-score)
purpose: Send the review queues of both RL runs to two reviewers. The reviewers' labels and the owner's contract decisions are ASSUMED inputs, written down as checklists before the run (tests/assumed_reviewers.py), because nobody reviewed anything in this build. From those inputs the platform measures inter-reviewer agreement per answer shape, turns agreed and settled labels into a human gold set, turns confirmed exploits into regression cases, gates the contract change the labels call for (math-final-answer@2.1.0), and re-scores the strict run with it.

checks.description: both reviewers returned a label for every queued item of both runs (assumed inputs, stored with their checklist line)
checks.because: vq.py submit uploads each reviewer's file; the labels job lists any queued item a reviewer did not label.

checks.description: the reviewers agree on plain numbers and disagree on at least one other answer shape, which is flagged as an unclear contract
checks.because: Their checklists read a plain number the same way; they read units, currency, mixed numbers and ratios differently.

checks.description: after the owner's decisions, agreed and settled labels form a human gold set, and the exploits people confirmed became regression cases
checks.because: A disagreement becomes a label only through a recorded decision for its slice; a training pass that people call wrong becomes a regression case.

checks.description: on the human gold set the old verifier accepts answers people call wrong; 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 accept none, and 2.1.0 accepts more correct ones than 2.0.0
checks.because: 2.1.0 differs from 2.0.0 only in what the box may hold: a unit, a currency sign or a mixed number, as the decisions said.

checks.description: the gate approves 2.1.0 with the reviewers' labels as evidence, and a training run can pin it
checks.because: The human check is that 2.1.0 accepts nothing the reviewers labelled wrong; the dry run checks the pins and creates nothing.

checks.description: re-scoring the strict run with 2.1.0 turns abstentions into passes, and no failure into a pass
checks.because: The new version only widens what the box may hold; every other rule is the same.

notes: Unclear slices: mixed_number, ratio. Labels settled by decision: 1. Exploits confirmed by the reviewers: 6. Re-score flips: {}.
